```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hughes_2023_chemotherapy_gcsf_anc"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hughes_2023_chemotherapy_gcsf_anc"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13019> (open access; Appendix S2 holds
  the NONMEM control stream of the final PKPD model)

Hughes et al. built a hybrid model to predict the next absolute neutrophil count
(ANC) during chemotherapy. A pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PKPD) model
supplies individual predictions and Bayesian parameter estimates as features to
an XGBoost regression model. This package ships the PKPD layer only. The
XGBoost models are trained on electronic health record data that are not
public, and they are not ODE models.

The PKPD layer is a Friberg myelosuppression model adapted to real-world data:

* **Chemotherapy** is a kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) input. Each dose is
  scaled to body surface area and divided by the training-population average
  dose of that drug, so a population-average dose has amount 1. Doses given
  within 24 h are combined into one dose whose amount is the mean of the
  normalized amounts. The dose enters a one-compartment state (`depot_kpd`)
  with fixed CL = 5 L/h and V = 50 L. The drug effect is linear,
  `Edrug = SLOPE * depot_kpd / V`.
* **G-CSF** (filgrastim or pegfilgrastim) is given subcutaneously into `depot`
  and absorbed into `central`. Absorption, clearance and bioavailability are
  fixed to the Melhem 2018 values and V is shared with the chemotherapy state.
  The G-CSF central *amount* adds `ST1 * central` to the proliferation rate and
  multiplies every bone-marrow transit rate by `1 + ST2 * central`.
* **Neutrophils** pass through `prol -> transit1 -> transit2 -> transit3 ->
  circ`, with `ktr = 4 / MTT`. The feedback term `(CIRC0 / circ)^gamma` acts
  only while `circ` is below baseline. The baseline CIRC0 is the observed
  pre-treatment ANC (floored at 0.5 x 10^9/L) times an exponential random
  effect.

# Population

The PKPD model was estimated on the training split (5952 patients, 21,831 ANC
observations) of a retrospective EHR cohort of 9121 adults treated with
chemotherapy at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center between 2016 and 2020
(Table 1). The training patients had metastatic breast cancer (3080), metastatic
thoracic cancer (2068: non-small cell, small cell or mesothelioma) or lymphoma
(804: diffuse large B-cell or follicular). Median age was 57.7 years (range
19.6-89.4), median weight 71 kg (28-187), and 75.8% were female. Self-reported
race was White in 74%, Asian in 9%, Black in 9%, and other or unknown in 8%.
Median serum albumin was 4.2 g/dL. Only the first three chemotherapy cycles of
each patient were used. 2923 training patients received G-CSF at least once.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Hughes_2023_chemotherapy_gcsf_anc")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value below appears in the final-estimate `$THETA` / `$OMEGA` / `$SIGMA`
blocks of the Appendix S2 control stream, whose `$PROBLEM` line reads "covs8,
final estimates". The control stream gives more digits than Table 2, and the
model uses those digits.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkel` (CLchemo / V) | 5 / 50 = 0.1 1/h, fixed | Table 2; Appendix S2 THETA(1), THETA(2) |
| `lvc` (V, shared by chemotherapy and G-CSF) | 50 L, fixed | Table 2; Appendix S2 `$PK` comment 'GCSF V fixed to same as chemo V' |
| `lka`, `e_peg_ka` | 0.123 1/h; x 0.1528455 for pegfilgrastim, fixed | Table 2; Appendix S2 `KSC = 0.123 * (0.1528455 ** PEG)` |
| `lcl`, `e_peg_cl` | 13.3 L/h; x 0.258 for pegfilgrastim, fixed | Table 2; Appendix S2 THETA(19) |
| `lfdepot`, `e_peg_fdepot` | 1; x 0.646 for pegfilgrastim, fixed | Table 2; Appendix S2 `F7 = 0.646 ** PEG` |
| `lslope` | 106.682 | Appendix S2 THETA(3); Table 2 SLOPE = 107 |
| `lmtt` | 126.246 h | Appendix S2 THETA(4); Table 2 MTT = 126 h |
| `lgamma` | 0.16, fixed | Table 2 (Kloft 2006 mean); Appendix S2 THETA(5) |
| `lstm1` (ST1) | 0.960093 | Appendix S2 THETA(20); Table 2 ST1 = 0.960 |
| `lstm2` (ST2) | 0.701233 | Appendix S2 THETA(21); Table 2 ST2 = 0.701 |
| `e_age_slope` | 0.751727 on (AGE / 57.2) | Appendix S2 THETA(27); Table 2 Sage |
| `e_age_stm1` | 0.160139 on (AGE / 57.2) | Appendix S2 THETA(28); Table 2 Page |
| `e_alb_mtt` | 0.325695 on (ALB / 4.1 g/dL) | Appendix S2 THETA(29); Table 2 Malb |
| Regimen effects on SLOPE | 0.26865-1.74323 | Appendix S2 THETA(6, 7, 9-14, 16); Table 2 Sdrug 0.269-1.74; Figure 2b |
| Regimen effects on MTT | 0.457641-1.88982 | Appendix S2 THETA(22-25); Table 2 Mdrug 0.458-1.89; Figure 2b |
| `etalslope`, `etalmtt`, `etalstm1` | 0.608128, 0.108427, 0.00997778 | Appendix S2 `$OMEGA`; Table 2 omega 78.0%, 32.9%, 9.99% |
| `etalcirc0` | 0.162848, fixed | Appendix S2 `CIRC0 = CIRCBL*EXP(ETA(3)*SIGMA(1,1)**0.5)`, `$OMEGA` 1 FIX |
| `expSd` | sqrt(0.162848) = 0.4035 | Appendix S2 `$SIGMA`, `Y = LOG(IPRED + FLAG) + EPS(1)`; Table 2 sigma 40.4% |
| ODE system and feedback | n/a | Appendix S2 `$DES`; Figure S1 |
| CIRC0 floor 0.5 x 10^9/L | n/a | Appendix S2 `IF(CIRCBL.LT.0.5) CIRCBL = 0.5` |

The regimen THETAs that the control stream fixes to 1 are not carried as
parameters. They are carboplatin + gemcitabine, gemcitabine + vinorelbine,
pemetrexed and vinorelbine on SLOPE, and paclitaxel on MTT. Patients on those
regimens have all regimen indicators at 0, which gives the identical
prediction.

# Regimen effects (Figure 2b)

The model's regimen multipliers must reproduce Figure 2b and the ranges in
Table 2.

```{r regimen-effects}
mod <- readModelDb("Hughes_2023_chemotherapy_gcsf_anc")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta

reg_tab <- tibble::tibble(par = names(th)[grepl("^e_trt_", names(th))]) |>
  mutate(
    parameter = ifelse(grepl("_slope$", par), "SLOPE", "MTT"),
    regimen = sub("^e_trt_(.*)_(slope|mtt)$", "\\1", par),
    multiplier = exp(unname(th[par]))
  )

# Table 2 reports the ranges Sdrug 0.269-1.74 and Mdrug 0.458-1.89.
rng <- reg_tab |>
  group_by(parameter) |>
  summarise(lo = min(multiplier), hi = max(multiplier))
stopifnot(
  abs(rng$lo[rng$parameter == "SLOPE"] - 0.269) < 0.0005,
  abs(rng$hi[rng$parameter == "SLOPE"] - 1.74) < 0.005,
  abs(rng$lo[rng$parameter == "MTT"] - 0.458) < 0.0005,
  abs(rng$hi[rng$parameter == "MTT"] - 1.89) < 0.005,
  sum(reg_tab$parameter == "SLOPE") == 9,
  sum(reg_tab$parameter == "MTT") == 4
)

reg_tab |>
  mutate(regimen = gsub("_", " + ", regimen)) |>
  ggplot(aes(multiplier, reorder(paste(regimen, "on", parameter), multiplier))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = "#1f77b4", size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Multiplier on the PD parameter", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the point estimates of Figure 2b of Hughes 2023."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Typical-value profiles

All five neutrophil compartments start at CIRC0. With no drug, the chain must
stay exactly at baseline, and a baseline ANC below 0.5 x 10^9/L must be raised
to 0.5.

```{r typical-setup}
trt_cols <- c(
  "TRT_CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE_DOXORUBICIN", "TRT_CARBOPLATIN_ETOPOSIDE",
  "TRT_CARBOPLATIN_PACLITAXEL", "TRT_CARBOPLATIN_PEMETREXED",
  "TRT_CISPLATIN_PEMETREXED", "TRT_CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE_FLUOROURACIL_METHOTREXATE",
  "TRT_DOCETAXEL", "TRT_GEMCITABINE", "TRT_PACLITAXEL"
)

# One subject: three 21-day cycles of a population-average chemotherapy dose
# (amount 1), optional G-CSF one day after each chemotherapy dose, and daily
# ANC observations on the circulating-neutrophil state.
make_subject <- function(id, regimen = "reference", gcsf = "none",
                         neut = 4.8, age = 57.2, alb = 41, chemo = TRUE) {
  cyc <- c(0, 504, 1008)
  dose <- if (chemo) {
    tibble(time = cyc, evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "depot_kpd")
  } else {
    tibble(time = numeric(0), evid = integer(0), amt = numeric(0), cmt = character(0))
  }
  if (gcsf != "none") {
    dose <- bind_rows(dose, tibble(time = cyc + 24, evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "depot"))
  }
  obs <- tibble(time = seq(0, 1512, by = 6), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "circ")
  ev <- bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(
      id = id, regimen = regimen, gcsf = gcsf,
      NEUT = neut, AGE = age, ALB = alb,
      FORM_GCSF_PEG = as.integer(gcsf == "pegfilgrastim")
    )
  for (tc in trt_cols) ev[[tc]] <- as.integer(regimen == tc)
  ev
}

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

```{r steady-state}
ev_ss <- bind_rows(
  make_subject(1, chemo = FALSE, neut = 4.8),
  make_subject(2, chemo = FALSE, neut = 0.3)
)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_ss, keep = "NEUT") |>
  as.data.frame()
ss <- sim_ss |>
  group_by(id, NEUT) |>
  summarise(min_anc = min(ANC), max_anc = max(ANC), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(ss, digits = 6, caption = "No-drug steady state (expected: max(NEUT, 0.5)).")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss$min_anc - pmax(ss$NEUT, 0.5)) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(ss$max_anc - pmax(ss$NEUT, 0.5)) < 1e-6)
)
```

The paper does not tabulate typical-value nadirs. The profiles below show how
each regimen group, and G-CSF for the reference group, changes the cycle-1
nadir of a typical patient (age 57.2 years, albumin 4.1 g/dL, baseline ANC 4.8
x 10^9/L).

```{r typical-profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
scen <- tibble(regimen = c("reference", trt_cols), gcsf = "none") |>
  bind_rows(tibble(regimen = "reference", gcsf = c("filgrastim", "pegfilgrastim")))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  make_subject(i, regimen = scen$regimen[i], gcsf = scen$gcsf[i])
}))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = c("regimen", "gcsf")) |>
  as.data.frame()

nadir_tab <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time < 504) |>
  group_by(regimen, gcsf) |>
  summarise(
    nadir = min(ANC),
    day_nadir = time[which.min(ANC)] / 24,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(regimen = sub("^TRT_", "", regimen)) |>
  arrange(nadir)
nadir_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen group" = regimen, "G-CSF" = gcsf,
    "Cycle-1 nadir (10^9/L)" = nadir, "Day of nadir" = day_nadir
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value cycle-1 ANC nadir by regimen group.")

ref_nadir <- nadir_tab |> filter(regimen == "reference", gcsf == "none")
peg_nadir <- nadir_tab |> filter(regimen == "reference", gcsf == "pegfilgrastim")
fil_nadir <- nadir_tab |> filter(regimen == "reference", gcsf == "filgrastim")
stopifnot(
  nrow(ref_nadir) == 1, nrow(peg_nadir) == 1, nrow(fil_nadir) == 1,
  # The Figure S2b observed median falls from about 5 to about 3 x 10^9/L
  # (ratio ~0.6) around day 8; the typical reference-regimen patient gives 0.58.
  ref_nadir$nadir / 4.8 > 0.45, ref_nadir$nadir / 4.8 < 0.75,
  ref_nadir$day_nadir > 7, ref_nadir$day_nadir < 12,
  # Deterministic (no random effects): G-CSF raises the nadir.
  peg_nadir$nadir > ref_nadir$nadir,
  fil_nadir$nadir > ref_nadir$nadir
)

sim_typ |>
  filter(gcsf == "none") |>
  mutate(regimen = sub("^TRT_", "", regimen)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, ANC, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "ANC (10^9/L)", colour = "Regimen group",
    caption = "Typical patient, population-average dose (amount 1) every 21 days."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 6))
```

The G-CSF effect per population-average dose is small: one dose of filgrastim
or pegfilgrastim raises the typical cycle-1 nadir by a few percent. The paper
also reports muted peaks and nadirs in individual predictions (Results, "Model
performance"). It suggests that the effects of G-CSF and of strongly
neutropenic regimens such as docetaxel were not separately identifiable,
because prophylactic G-CSF is usually prescribed with those regimens
(Discussion).

# Visual predictive check (Figure S2b)

Figure S2b compares the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of observed ANC with
simulated data against time after cycle start. The observed patients' regimen
mix is not published, so the virtual cohort below draws each patient's regimen
group with equal probability from the nine groups and the reference group. It
also draws age and albumin around the Table 1 medians. Baseline ANC is drawn
log-normally around the Table 1 median ANC of 4.8 x 10^9/L.

```{r vpc-cohort}
set.seed(2023)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
n_vpc <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_vpc),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_vpc, 57.7, 12), 20), 89),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_vpc, 42, 4), 17), 53),
  NEUT = exp(rnorm(n_vpc, log(4.8), 0.35)),
  FORM_GCSF_PEG = 0L,
  regimen = sample(c("reference", trt_cols), n_vpc, replace = TRUE)
)
for (tc in trt_cols) cohort[[tc]] <- as.integer(cohort$regimen == tc)

ev_vpc <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = c(0, 504, 1008)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "depot_kpd"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, time = seq(0, 1512, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "circ")
) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_vpc[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r vpc-figure, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  mutate(day = (time %% 504) / 24) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(day)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "#1f77b4", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after cycle start (days)", y = "ANC (k/uL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles (with residual error), three",
      "21-day cycles pooled. Compare with Figure S2b of Hughes 2023."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Centre of the distribution only (robust to which subjects land in the tails).
# Figure S2b: observed median about 5 at cycle start and about 3 at days 7-10.
med_start <- vpc$p50[vpc$day == 0]
med_nadir <- min(vpc$p50[vpc$day >= 6 & vpc$day <= 12])
stopifnot(
  length(med_start) == 1,
  med_start > 3, med_start < 7,
  med_nadir > 2, med_nadir < 4.5,
  med_nadir < med_start
)
```

The simulated median falls from about `r round(med_start, 1)` to about
`r round(med_nadir, 1)` x 10^9/L between days 6 and 12, close to the observed
median in Figure S2b (about 5 falling to about 3 around day 8). The observed
5th percentile falls lower (about 0.4 x 10^9/L near day 8) than the simulated
one. The virtual cohort gives no G-CSF and spreads patients evenly over the
regimen groups, so it is a qualitative check of the model's shape, not a
reconstruction of the test set.

# G-CSF pharmacokinetics (PKNCA)

The control stream states that the fixed G-CSF clearance was chosen to give
the Melhem 2018 half-lives: 2.6 h for filgrastim and 10.1 h for pegfilgrastim,
with V = 50 L. After a subcutaneous dose the terminal phase is
absorption-limited (flip-flop): the absorption half-life is 5.6 h for
filgrastim and 36.9 h for pegfilgrastim. The elimination half-life is
therefore checked with PKNCA on a bolus placed directly into the G-CSF central
compartment.

```{r gcsf-pknca}
ev_pk <- bind_rows(lapply(c(filgrastim = 0L, pegfilgrastim = 1L), function(peg) {
  bind_rows(
    tibble(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 1, cmt = "central"),
    tibble(time = c(0, seq(0.25, 120, by = 0.25)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(
      id = peg + 1L, FORM_GCSF_PEG = peg,
      treatment = ifelse(peg == 1L, "pegfilgrastim", "filgrastim")
    )
})) |>
  mutate(NEUT = 4.8, AGE = 57.2, ALB = 41)
for (tc in trt_cols) ev_pk[[tc]] <- 0L

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  events = ev_pk, keep = "treatment", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(Cc = central / 50)

conc_pk <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
dose_pk <- ev_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)

nca_pk <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_pk, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_pk, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, half.life = TRUE)
))

published_pk <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~half.life,
  "filgrastim", 2.6,
  "pegfilgrastim", 10.1
)
pk_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_pk,
  reference = published_pk,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  pk_cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "G-CSF elimination half-life, simulated (PKNCA) vs. the Appendix S2",
    "control-stream comment. * differs by >20%."
  )
)

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_pk$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life")
hl_fil <- hl$PPORRES[hl$treatment == "filgrastim"]
hl_peg <- hl$PPORRES[hl$treatment == "pegfilgrastim"]
stopifnot(
  length(hl_fil) == 1, length(hl_peg) == 1,
  abs(hl_fil / 2.6 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(hl_peg / 10.1 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **XGBoost layer not included.** The ML, enriched and augmented models of the
  paper are tree ensembles trained on non-public data. Only their PKPD
  backbone, which is fully specified in Appendix S2, is shipped.
- **Dose units are normalized.** The paper normalized every dose to the
  training-population average dose of that drug after BSA scaling, but does
  not report those average doses. Users therefore supply normalized amounts
  (1 = population-average dose). The paper states this normalization for
  "each dose for each medication". The maintainers applied it to G-CSF as well,
  because ST1 and ST2 act on the G-CSF central amount: an amount in micrograms
  would make proliferation grow several thousand-fold after one dose.
- **Chemotherapy is a K-PD state.** The control stream names compartment 1
  "CENTR", but the data contained no drug concentrations and CL and V are
  fixed (Results, "PKPD model development"), so the state is encoded as the
  registered `depot_kpd`. Its elimination rate is `kel = CLchemo / V = 0.1
  1/h`.
- **Regimen indicators.** The NONMEM `REG` code is replaced by nine mutually
  exclusive `TRT_<regimen>` indicators, one per estimated regimen group. Each
  indicator covers the cytotoxic backbone with or without monoclonal antibodies
  or immunotherapy, following the regimen-to-THETA mapping of Appendix S2 (the
  full code lists are in the model's `covariateData` notes). Regimens whose
  THETA was fixed to 1, regimens given to fewer than 50 training patients, and
  any regimen not listed take all indicators at 0.
- **Baseline random effect.** NONMEM writes CIRC0 as `CIRCBL * exp(ETA(3) *
  sqrt(SIGMA))` with `OMEGA(3) = 1 FIX`, so the baseline eta has the residual
  variance (Dansirikul method). The model encodes it as `etalcirc0 ~
  fixed(0.162848)`, which gives the same distribution. If the residual variance
  is re-estimated, `etalcirc0` must be updated to match it by hand.
- **Residual error.** `Y = LOG(IPRED + 0.00001) + EPS(1)` is encoded as
  `lnorm(expSd)`. The 1e-5 offset only matters at ANC values far below the
  data range and is omitted.
- **Covariate units.** Serum albumin is supplied in g/L (the canonical column)
  and converted to g/dL inside the model. Baseline ANC (`NEUT`) is supplied in
  10^9/L, the paper's unit.
- **Virtual cohort.** The regimen mix, the baseline ANC spread (log-SD 0.35)
  and the absence of G-CSF in the VPC cohort are assumptions. Table 1 reports
  only cancer type, G-CSF use and summary demographics.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-10-28.
